blocks.text: Optimize your Slack setup on mac

Your Mac is your primary tool for sales. Keeping Slack running smoothly is essential. First, ensure you are on the latest version. Slack requires macOS 14 or higher for full support. If the app feels sluggish, go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This often fixes performance issues caused by long sessions.

Speed matters when you are juggling multiple deals. Use Command + / to open the cheat sheet. Learn Command + K to jump between channels and direct messages. This saves you from clicking through the sidebar. Use Shift + Enter to create a new line in a message without sending it. This is helpful for drafting structured updates for your manager.

items: Command + K: Open the quick switcher to find any conversation.
Command + F: Search within your current channel.
Command + ,: Open your preferences to manage notification sounds.
Command + B: Bold text to highlight key deal metrics.

blocks.text: Sales reps often get overwhelmed by pings. Go to Preferences > Notifications to set a schedule. You can pause notifications entirely during your deep work hours. Use the /dnd command to quickly silence alerts when you start a demo. This keeps you focused on your prospect.

Searching in Slack is a core skill. Use modifiers to narrow down your results. Type from: @name to find messages from a specific colleague. Use has: link to find shared documents. This prevents you from scrolling through hundreds of messages to find a contract or a link.

When working on a deal, use threads to keep discussions organized. Reply in a thread instead of starting a new message in the channel. This keeps the main channel clean for everyone. Pin important messages like deal terms or account details to the channel header. This makes them easy for the whole team to find.
Integrating Slack with your sales tools

Many sales tools offer Slack integrations. You can get notifications from your CRM directly in Slack. Avoid connecting too many tools at once. This creates noise. Only enable notifications for high-priority events like deal closed-won or new leads.

Researching prospects takes time. If you find a useful article, share it in your team channel. Use the saved items feature to keep track of interesting threads. Click the bookmark icon to save a message for later. You can view all saved items by clicking the saved button in your sidebar.

Do not use @channel unless it is urgent. This creates unnecessary distractions for the entire team. Use @here instead if you only need to reach people who are currently active. Be clear and concise in your messages. If a conversation takes more than five minutes, suggest a huddle or a meeting.

Keep your sidebar organized. You can group channels into sections. Right-click a section to rename it. This helps you separate your internal team channels from your project-specific channels. It keeps your workspace tidy and helps you find what you need faster.

faq.question: How do I clear the Slack cache on Mac?
faq.answer: Go to the Help menu in the top bar, select Troubleshooting, then choose Clear Cache and Restart.

faq.question: What is the best way to find old messages?
faq.answer: Use the search bar with modifiers like from: or has: to filter results quickly.

faq.question: Can I use Slack on older Macs?
faq.answer: Slack requires macOS 14 or above. Check your system version in the Apple menu under About This Mac.
